commit.message:
docs(community): say who can open GitHub Discussions and what they are for (#3573)

**Before:** The Channels table on the Communication page lists GitHub
Discussions for "Ideas, feature requests with rationale, questions,
roadmap discussion, announcements and releases, and meeting agendas and
notes".

**After:** The row lists meeting agendas and notes, in the Meeting Notes
categories, and announcements. It says only people with write access to
the repository can open a discussion, and it sends ideas, feature
requests and questions to Discord.

## Why

Two changes to Discussions in this repository are not on the page.

- On 2026-09-02 an announcement in `#general` on the contributor Discord
said: "We are disabling GitHub Discussions for those without write
permissions in the repo ... we turned those off for public creation.
Contributors can still use those for meeting notes."
- On 2026-09-25 the existing threads outside meeting notes were closed
with the comment "We've limited Discussions in this repository to
meeting notes and are closing this thread. To continue the conversation,
pick a channel from Contributor Communication"
([example](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/discussions/3225#discussioncomment-18603053)).
That comment sends readers to this page, and this page sends them back
to Discussions.

Checked on 2026-11-21:

- 566 discussions were closed between 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-26.
- All 24 discussions opened since 2026-09-26 are in a Meeting Notes
category, each opened by an organization member.
- The open discussions outside Meeting Notes are two announcements and
one thread in Ideas - Transports.

## Question for review

The two statements differ. The announcement restricts who can open a
discussion. The closing comment says Discussions are limited to meeting
notes. The row follows current practice (meeting notes and
announcements) and states the access rule. If members are meant to open
other kinds of discussion, the row should say so.

## Not changed

These passages still send work to Discussions. They hold for people with
write access, so this PR leaves them. They read differently for everyone
else.

- Communication, Decision records: "A Discord discussion heading toward
a technical or governance decision must move to a GitHub Discussion."
- Working Groups and Interest Groups, Meetings and channels: "Long-form
technical discussion goes to GitHub Discussions, which are triaged
weekly, and a group may have its own Discussions category on request."
- Working Groups and Interest Groups, Reporting: quarterly updates are
posted "as a document in its GitHub Discussions category".

The Communication page says it "is changed by a Process SEP". This PR
treats the row as a correction to match current practice. If a
maintainer reads it as a rule change, it should go through a Process
SEP.

## Checks

`prettier --check` passes on the edited file. The longer cell widens the
table, so the diff touches all seven table rows. `npm run prep` was not
run.

commit.message:
docs: align FSIG charter with problem-first, WG-led governance (#3572)

## Summary
Proposes an amendment to the Financial Services Interest Group charter
to make problem identification, sharing existing MCP implementation
approaches, and routing unresolved needs to WGs the default path.

- Preserve exploratory solution discussions, prototypes, and extension
work where useful for validating requirements.
- Prefer existing MCP primitives and existing WG efforts over
duplicating solution development within FSIG.
- For substantial gaps without a relevant WG, gather cross-IG/community
support and potential contributors for a new WG proposal; this is not a
new mandatory cross-IG approval requirement.
- Clarify that SEP sponsorship comes from a WG or exceptionally Core
Maintainers, not FSIG itself.

## Governance references
- [Working Groups and Interest Groups
(SEP-2149)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-interest-groups)
- [WG formation and charter amendment
rules](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-interest-groups#amending-or-retiring-a-group)
- [SEP
Guidelines](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/sep-guidelines)
- [SEP
template](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/seps/TEMPLATE.md)

**Governance:** This is a proposed charter amendment by an FSIG
Facilitator and requires Core Maintainer approval. It does not claim to
amend MCP-wide governance.

**AI assistance disclosure:** AI assistance was used to draft and edit
this documentation change; the proposing facilitator reviewed the
intended scope and governance alignment.

chats and dots only. |
| MCPJam | ✓ | Source on `main`

| TanStack AI | Not listed (no existing row; supports webhook only) |

Cross-checked against the [field report in

commit.message:
sep(SEP-3415): Events Extension (#3415)

Defines Events, an extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/events`) that
lets an MCP client subscribe to things that happen in an upstream
system, such as a Slack message, a repository push or a PagerDuty
incident, and have an agent react without the user being present.

- A server lists event types with `events/list`: a name, an
`inputSchema` for subscription arguments, a `payloadSchema`, and the
delivery modes it supports.
- Three delivery modes, none mandatory: poll (`events/poll`), push (a
long-lived `events/stream`), and webhook (`events/subscribe`, signed per
Standard Webhooks, with a refreshed TTL).
- Opaque cursors let a client resume after a disconnect. Replay is
optional per event type, and `truncated: true` signals skipped events.

This is the [design
sketch](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-triggers-events/blob/main/docs/design-sketch-proposal.md)
from the Triggers & Events Working Group, discussed in its weekly
meetings, written in SEP format. To fit the `2026-07-28` protocol, the
capability moves under `extensions`, `list_changed` rides on a
`subscriptions/listen` filter field, and results carry `resultType`.

For reviewers:

- The SEP requests five general-purpose error codes. The numbers
(`-32023` to `-32027`) are provisional.
- The reference implementation in an official SDK is outstanding.
- Open Questions lists eight items, including whether to fold these
errors into `InvalidParams`.

Verified with `prettier --check`, and every in-page link resolves to a
heading. The file keeps its `0000-` name, so `render-seps` skips it.

**AI assistance:** an AI coding assistant restructured the design sketch
into SEP format and aligned it with the current protocol. The design,
design decisions and review are by @pja-ant.

docs(inspector): add load testing and Active Sessions docs (#3503)

Adds a dedicated **Load testing** page, and an **Active sessions**
section on the web client page. The load mode is run by the web client's
Load test panel, the CLI (`--load`) and mcpdo (`tools/call --load`) on
one shared engine. Active Sessions is a new web-client view of every
session the backend holds open, with a way to end one
(modelcontextprotocol/inspector#2901). Before this, the flags were
listed only inside a dense CI-gates bullet on the CLI page and in one
sentence on the mcpdo page (from #3483). Tracked in
modelcontextprotocol/inspector#2869. Both doc versions (`draft` and
`2026-07-28`) change identically, apart from their link prefixes.

## What changed

| Page | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/inspector/load-testing` (new) | An overview of the three front
ends, then: **In the web client**, with five screenshots (the Load test
button, the form, a run in progress, a tool summary, and a scenario
stepped over three concurrency levels); **From the command line**, with
a core flag table and a topic table for the rest; **The summary** (the
three output shapes, each field, p50–p999 and the bounded histogram, the
`--load-rate` fields, `stoppedEarly`, the mode-specific blocks); then
**Watching a run**, **Saving every call**, **Varying the arguments**,
**Scenarios**, **Stepped and ramped load**, **Open loop**, **When a run
fails or stops**, **Thresholds** (all five, exit `10`), **Comparing
against a baseline**, **Multiple sessions**, **Session churn**,
**Notification fan-out**, **Multiple generator processes**
(`--load-workers`), and **On an mcpdo connection** (runs inside the
daemon, files read by `mcpdo`, later commands queue, Ctrl+C,
`connection_lost` / `consecutive_errors`, extra sessions, elicitations).
|
| `tools/inspector/cli` | A short **Load testing a tool** section with
one example, the exit behavior, and a link to the new page. The
exit-code `10` row and the CI-gates bullet now link to the new page. |
| `tools/inspector/mcpdo` | A short **Load testing** section with one
example and a link to the new page's mcpdo section. |
| `tools/inspector/web` | A short **Load testing** subsection under
Tools, linking to the new page's web section. A new **Active sessions**

docs: align the extensions overview with SEP-3392 (#3565)

SEP-3392 (Extension Lifecycle) asks for `docs/extensions/overview.mdx`
to be updated to match it once it reaches Final. The overview already
follows the SEP's structure, but several details had drifted from the
final text. This PR brings them back in line.

## Changes

- **Experimental entry**: the stage table now also covers any Maintainer
creating an `experimental-ext-` repository, matching the SEP's stage
table and its Experimental section.
- **Skipping Beta**: notes that the Core Maintainers can waive the Beta
requirement by a recorded vote (SEP-3392, "An extension MUST NOT skip
Beta, unless…").
- **Stage changes**: the Evolution section now says a stage change is
the one change a Core Maintainer approves, matching the SEP's rules for
moving between stage directories.
- **`revision` setting**: moved out of the Beta bullet so it covers both
Experimental and Beta, and adds the SEP's rules that an absent
`revision` means the initial revision and that a peer should not enable
an extension when it receives a `revision` it doesn't know ("Identifiers
and compatibility").
- **Experimental ground rules**: the README requirement applies to the
`experimental-ext-` repository, and the naming requirement to published
packages, as SEP-2133 states them.
- **Repository layout**: notes that repositories that predate the
lifecycle are still moving to the stage-directory layout. Today
`ext-skills` and `ext-auth` have moved, and `ext-apps` and `ext-tasks`
have not.
- **Experimental repositories**: lists the current `experimental-ext-`
repositories.

`ext-events` is left out of that list on purpose. It is the renamed
`experimental-ext-triggers-events` repository, and the Events extension
it incubated was accepted as SEP-3415 (#3415). Events should be added to
this page as a Beta extension, with its intended destination, once its
specification is published.

## Verification

- Checked each change against `seps/3392-extension-lifecycle.md` and
`seps/2133-extensions.md`, and checked the repository claims against the
current `modelcontextprotocol` organization repositories.
- `npm run prep` passes with no warnings or errors.

claim against SEP-3392 and the current repositories, reviewed the
changes and the findings myself, and decided to leave out `ext-events`.

feat(blog): add a quote block for person quotes (#3563)

Long quotations from named people were written as plain blockquotes:
italic text in quotation marks behind a bar, with a `✦ **Name**, Title,
Company` line underneath. In the first anniversary post, eleven of them
in a row read as a wall of text.

## What changes

- **`quote` shortcode on its own** now renders a quote block: a panel on
`--surface` in the text column, with a large opening quotation mark cut
by the top edge and a closing one cut by the bottom edge, both one step
darker than the panel and behind the words. The quote is upright body
text without quotation marks of its own. The attribution is set like the
post byline (name at step 2, role at step 1).
- **Inside a `quotes` block** the shortcode is unchanged and still
renders a carousel card.
- **New parameter `url`** links the company name. `title` accepts
markdown in a quote block, for people with two affiliations. `logo` is
optional and sits under the role.
- **First anniversary post**: its eleven quotes use the new block.

```
{{< quote name="Ada Person" title="CTO" company="Acme" url="https://acme.example" >}}
Quote text, markdown allowed.
{{< /quote >}}
```

Only existing design tokens are used, so the block follows the light and
dark themes, and the marks scale with the page title on phones.

## Wording changes in the anniversary post

Converting the quotes removed the surrounding quotation marks and
italics. Three quotes also changed slightly:

- Block: removed the press-release fragment `" said Dhanji R. Prasanna,
CTO of Block. "` from the middle of the quote.
- Google Cloud and PulseMCP: removed a stray closing quotation mark.
- Obot AI: added the missing full stop at the end.

## Test plan

- `hugo` builds without warnings.
- Checked the block in light and dark at desktop width and at 390px.
- The anniversary post renders eleven quote blocks, and the 2026-07-28
post's carousel still renders its cards.
- Not run locally: Prettier and the repository's `npm run prep` checks.

commit.message:
docs: stop presenting deprecated features as current on the spec overview pages (#3552)

The architecture and base protocol overview pages are where many people
new to MCP start. Both still presented sampling, roots and logging as
current features, with no indication that they are deprecated as of
`2026-07-28` (SEP-2577).

Fixes #3548

## Architecture page

Builds on the branch Lazzaretti proposed in #3548 (their commit is
included as-is), which updates the five places the issue lists:

- Intro: "context exchange and sampling coordination" becomes "context
exchange"
- Host: "Coordinates AI/LLM integration and sampling" becomes
"Coordinates AI/LLM integration"
- Servers: elicitation is the example of client input
- Capability Negotiation: clients "declare capabilities like elicitation
handling"
- Sequence diagram: the `InputRequiredResult` example is
`elicitation/create`, with the host asking the user for input

On top of that, the Servers bullet reads "Request client input (e.g.
elicitation)" and carries a footnote saying sampling and roots requests
are also delivered via `InputRequiredResult` but are deprecated and
should not be used in new implementations, linking to the Deprecated
Features registry.

## Base protocol overview

- Client Features: "Elicitation provided by clients; sampling and root
directory lists are deprecated", linking to the registry
- Utilities: examples are argument completion and pagination, followed
by "logging is deprecated", linking to the registry
- Message Patterns: the MRTR summary uses "(e.g. elicitation)" as its
example of client input

The component list is an enumeration, so the deprecated features stay
listed and are labelled inline. The architecture page only gives an
example, so there they move to a footnote.

## Released revision

The same changes are applied to the `2026-07-28` copies of both pages,
which were identical to draft apart from link paths. Links there point
at the `2026-07-28` pages.

## Not included

The reserved `_meta` key tables on the base protocol overview still list
`io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` without a deprecation marker. Those
rows link to the Logging page, which carries the deprecation notice.

## Verification

- `npm run prep` passes
- Footnote syntax is already rendered by the docs site on the SEP pages
(for example SEP-2567), and the generated "Footnotes" heading does not
appear in the table of contents

---------

Co-authored-by: Fabrizio Lazzaretti <fabrizio@lazzaretti.me>
